ing: scotch bonnet or habanero, left whole
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for a few minutes per batch, then set it aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pot for [[5 minutes]] until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick paste, about 5 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot with [[4 cups]] water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladleful of the hot broth in a bowl until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Add the pumpkin and the whole chili. Simmer uncovered for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender and the oil rises to the top.
While the stew cooks, rinse [[2 cups]] rice until the water runs clearer. Boil it with [[4 cups]] water and a pinch of salt, covered on low heat, for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Taste the stew and add salt. Remove the whole chili (or mash a little in for more heat).
Fluff the rice and spoon the domoda over it.
Season the fish with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and fry the fish for 2 minutes per side, then set aside.
In the same oil, cook the chopped onion and garlic for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and chopped tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and oily.
Pour in [[4.5 cups]] water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and the whole chili, and bring to a boil.
Add the carrots, eggplant and cabbage. Simmer for 15 minutes until just tender, then lift the vegetables and fish pieces out onto a plate, leaving the broth.
Add the rinsed rice to the broth, stir once, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Lay the fried fish and vegetables on top of the rice, cover and steam for 10 minutes more.
Fluff the rice gently, remove the chili, and serve topped with the fish and vegetables.
In a big bowl, mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Add the sliced onions and chicken and toss well.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least [[2 hours]], or overnight if you can.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, keeping the onions and liquid. Pat the chicken dry.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for about 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Add the marinated onions to the pot with the chili. Cook on medium for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Return the chicken, pour in [[0.5 cup]] water and the remaining salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Meanwhile rinse [[2 cups]] rice and cook it with [[4 cups]] water and a pinch of salt, covered on low heat, for 15 minutes.
Serve the chicken and sticky onion sauce over the rice.
Heat the palm oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions and garlic for [[6 minutes]] until soft.
Add [[3 cups]] water, the whole chili, the dried shrimp if using, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil.
Add the fish chunks, lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes until the fish is just cooked.
Stir in the sliced okra. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the stew is thick and slippery.
Meanwhile rinse [[2 cups]] rice and boil it with [[4 cups]] water and salt, covered on low heat, for 15 minutes.
Taste the stew and add salt. Remove the chili.
Serve the superkanja over the rice.

ing: frozen cassava leaves, or fresh spinach
smoked fish or fresh white fish
st: Put the beef, half the onion, garlic and [[4 cups]] water in a large pot with a little salt. Boil, then simmer covered for 40 minutes.
If using frozen cassava leaves, thaw them. Chop the greens finely, or blend them with a splash of water.
Add the greens and the whole chili to the pot. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
In a small pan, heat the palm oil and cook the remaining onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir the onions and oil into the pot. Mix the peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, and stir that in too.
Add the fish in chunks. Simmer for 20 minutes until the greens are very tender and the oil floats on top.
Season with salt, remove the chili, and serve hot with rice.

ing: seeded, minced, or 0.5 tsp chili flakes
for blending, plus more for soaking
st: Soak the peas in plenty of water for [[1 hour]] until they swell.
Rub the peas between your hands in the water so the skins loosen and float. Pour off the skins and repeat a few times.
Drain the peas and blend them with the onion, chili and about [[0.5 cup]] water into a thick, fluffy paste. Add water a spoonful at a time only if needed.
Beat the batter hard with a spoon for 2 minutes to whip in air, then stir in the salt.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Scoop a tablespoon of batter and slide it into the oil. Fry 4 or 5 at a time for 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with hot sauce or bread.
Rinse the dried hibiscus flowers under cold water.
Bring [[8 cups]] water to a boil in a large pot.
Add the hibiscus and ginger, turn off the heat, cover and steep for [[20 minutes]].
Strain the liquid into a pitcher and discard the flowers.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar while it is warm until dissolved. Taste and add more if you like it sweeter.
Add the mint and lime juice if using. Chill for at least 2 hours and serve over ice.
